19 November 2026 # HSBC RedCoin expands into wealth with tokenised fund access - Minimum subscription of HKD 100 (funded with RCHKD 100) 1 via HSBC HK Mobile Banking App, with potentially faster settlement 2 Hong Kong, 19 November 2026 — HSBC RedCoin (Ticker: RCHKD), HSBC’s Hong Kong dollar-denominated stablecoin, is now available on the HSBC HK Mobile Banking App (the App). Eligible customers will now be able to activate their stablecoin wallet in the App and use RCHKD to access a new tokenised unit class (Class SD) 3 of the HSBC Global Money Funds – Hong Kong Dollar (the Fund) 4. By embedding tokenised funds into the App which customers are already familiar with, HSBC RedCoin is now extended from day-to-day payments into wealth management. Winnie Ng, Head of Wealth and Premier Solutions, Hong Kong, HSBC, said: “Tokenised funds reduce traditional market friction and enable faster settlement. By bringing HSBC RedCoin together with tokenised investments, we are creating new ways for our wealth customers to access innovative investment opportunities with a lower entry threshold and a more efficient experience. This is an important step in broadening our digital wealth proposition, and we will continue to expand the range of tokenised investment products available to our customers.” Launched in 1991, the Fund is managed by HSBC Asset Management. Its dividend distributions are separate from HSBC RedCoin, which pays no interest. Jasmine Hung, CEO, HSBC Asset Management, Hong Kong, said: “We are delighted to launch a tokenised unit class of our long-standing Hong Kong dollar money market fund, offering investors a new digital gateway to an established fund. This launch marks an exciting step forward, and we look forward to continuing our collaboration with all stakeholders to support the development of the digital asset investment ecosystem and delivering a more diverse range of solutions to our customers as the market evolves.” The launch responds to clear customer interest in practical applications for digital assets. HSBC’s Hong Kong stablecoin study found that digital asset trading and tokenised investments were the most widely recognised use case, cited by 57 per cent of respondents. HSBC’s Securities Services tokenises the new unit class, while its Digital Assets Custody capability provides safekeeping services for HSBC RedCoin and the tokenised unit class (Class SD) of the Fund. ... 1. HSBC RedCoin is redeemable 1:1 for HKD. 2. Actual settlement time depends when the investment order is placed, subject to the Fund’s deal arrangements. 3. Class SD is denominated in Hong Kong dollar. 4. Subscriptions to the Fund can be made by HSBC RedCoin holders, with HSBC converting the HSBC RedCoin into the equivalent amount of HKD for subscription.

# HSBC expands credit facility for China’s low-carbon sectors to $8bn 17 Nov 2026 We’ve doubled the size of our Sustainability and Transition Credit Facility to $8 billion to help businesses operating in the Chinese mainland’s low-carbon and clean energy sectors to grow and expand globally. As well as increasing the size of the facility, we’re broadening our financial support to international businesses operating in the Chinese mainland in these sectors, empowering them to advance their own transition efforts. Since its launch in May, the facility has successfully supported a diverse range of sustainable transactions across key sectors. They include: - A €185 million (US$204 million) financing facility for EVE Energy and Sinosure for the development of a large-scale, lithium-ion battery manufacturing plant in Hungary - A landmark RMB745 million (US$111 million) aviation finance and transition loan for China Eastern Airlines – our first RMB-denominated facility of its kind in Asia - Guarantees enabling major infrastructure development in the Middle East ## Supporting the transition The dedicated credit facility offers financing to eligible businesses in the transition ecosystem operating in a range of sectors, including clean power, electrification of transport, data centres and artificial intelligence. Through the facility, HSBC increases credit limits for eligible companies, streamlines credit approvals and develops tailored financial solutions to help bring clean technologies and solutions to markets more efficiently. Chaoni Huang, Asia Head of Sustainable Finance and Transition at HSBC, said: “We look forward to supporting more companies as they expand overseas and navigate their own transition in the Chinese mainland. “HSBC’s global reach and market expertise make us well placed to navigate this opportunity.”

# Our strategy - built on trust, accelerated with AI By Georges Elhedery, Group CEO, HSBC 18 Nov 2026 Banking is entering a new operating environment. Artificial intelligence is changing how customers make decisions, how businesses operate and how financial services are delivered. At HSBC, our colleagues are using AI to simplify processes, improve efficiency and create more personalised experiences. Payments, investing and treasury services are becoming faster, more intelligent and increasingly real time. Crucially, AI is beginning to accelerate delivery of our strategy and ambition, enabling us to move at pace and put customers at the heart of everything we do. ... We’re empowering relationship managers with AI to help them serve customers faster, while personalising the experience through ... We’re investing in the technology and platforms that strengthen how we serve customers, and giving colleagues the tools and training to adapt, succeed and benefit from the opportunities AI brings. ... November 19, 2026 ## E-commerce business profitability improved significantly, with quick commerce narrowing losses while maintaining market share Alibaba Group reported faster cloud growth and higher cloud profitability for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, as its full-stack AI strategy drives monetization from rising customer adoption of cloud services and AI-related products across industries. Group revenue rose 10% year-over-year, while adjusted EBITA increased 260%, driven primarily by improved results in Taobao Instant Commerce and Cloud business, as well as operating efficiencies across various businesses. “We will continue to bring technological innovations to our comprehensive AI stack to meet the strong and diverse AI demands across industries,” said Eddie Wu, Chief Executive Officer of Alibaba Group. Broader Industry AI Adoption Drives Cloud Growth and Increased Margins AI Cloud and Compute Services revenue climbed 53% year-over-year to RMB60,973 million (US$9,094 million), with revenue from external customers up 64%. AI-related product revenue delivered triple-digit year-over-year growth for the thirteenth consecutive quarter. Cloud segment adjusted EBITA increased 121% year-over-year to RMB8,838 million (US$1,318 million), with quality earnings lifting margins to 14.5%. The results reflect broad-based demand for Alibaba’s AI + cloud services beyond training and inference workloads at AI labs. Customers across the internet, automotive, embodied AI, financial services and biotechnology sectors rapidly expanded their use of Alibaba’s cloud services to support innovation and business growth. To support this increasingly diverse demand, Alibaba continued to strengthen its full-stack AI capabilities during the quarter. T-Head unveiled its next-generation Zhenwu V900 chip for AI training and inference, with commercial release scheduled for the first quarter of 2027. Alongside infrastructure advances, Alibaba continued to prioritize foundation model development, releasing Qwen4-Max on November 16 to support complex work, creativity and research tasks. Bringing AI Agents into Work and Everyday Life Alibaba is extending AI monetization through agents for enterprise workflows, merchant operations and consumers’ daily life. QwenWork, Alibaba’s one-stop AI agent platform, helps enterprises carry out business tasks through AI agents that draw on company documents, meeting records, and internal communications. QwenWork E-commerce, launched in October, is designed to automate store operations and customer service for merchants. For consumers, the Qwen app supports everyday tasks from shopping to travel, while Qwen Go!, a personal agent added in October, carries out multi-step tasks across platforms. Commerce Performance Improves as Quick Commerce Losses Narrow Alibaba’s E-commerce business benefited from solid marketplace performance as Taobao Instant Commerce narrowed losses while maintaining market share. Adjusted EBITA increased 243% year-over-year, primarily driven by a significant loss reduction in the China Quick Commerce business with stable China e-commerce operating profit, narrower international e-commerce losses, and strong profits in global wholesale. Customer management revenue declined 5% year-over-year and increased 1% on a like-for-like basis. The number of 88VIP members, Alibaba’s highest-spending consumer cohort, continued to grow at a double-digit rate year-over-year to reach around 66 million, underscoring the depth of engagement among its most valuable customers. Executing the Next Phase of AI Growth Alibaba is expanding its AI infrastructure to meet the strong demand from AI labs and China’s emerging innovation economy. Greater scale enables more flexible, efficient, and cost-effective computing. Through continued investment, Alibaba aims to extend scale leadership, strengthen its supply chain and reinforce its long-term competitive position. “As AI monetization continues to ramp up, we will maintain disciplined investments in AI capabilities with a focus on return on invested capital while targeting to achieve positive free cash flow,” said Toby Xu, Chief Financial Officer of Alibaba Group. Alibaba ended the quarter with RMB487,929 million (US$72,776 million) in cash and other liquid investments. It also repurchased approximately 17.95 million ordinary shares for a total of US$221 million, affirming its commitment to returning capital to shareholders alongside its investment.

Investing.com-- Alibaba’s Hong Kong shares rose on Friday as stronger-than-expected second fiscal quarter revenue invited some bargain buying into the battered Chinese tech giant. Alibaba Group (HK: 9988) rose as much as 2.7% to HK$83.15, outpacing an over 2% slump in the Hang Seng index. The stock rose after hitting a near two-year low on Thursday. The e-commerce giant on Thursday reported stronger-than-expected revenue for the quarter to September 30, aided by improving returns from artificial intelligence cloud and computing services. Adjusted profit also rose sharply in the quarter, aided by some improvement in margins and narrower losses in the company’s growing quick-commerce business. The earnings print helped restore some confidence in Alibaba, whose shares were battered by mounting concerns over the company’s access to offshore advanced AI chips, which was effectively cut off by new U.S. restrictions this week. Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu said the company’s 2030 targets of $100 billion in external cloud revenue and 20% EBITDA margin remained on track, despite the new restrictions. The company is also facing a shareholder class action lawsuit over allegations that it hid its ties to a suspected Chinese spy who was involved with Nvidia. Alibaba’s gains on Friday came amid a broader rout in tech and AI stocks, amid mounting questions over the long-term returns from the technology. Frontier AI lab Anthropic’s bumper market debut on Thursday did little to lift sentiment towards the sector. Alibaba, along with peers Baidu and Tencent, is regarded as being at the forefront of China’s AI development efforts. But this has left the stock exposed to a deep rout in AI valuations since October.

# AIA Hong Kong & Macau launches Omni Healthcare Circle to promote affordable and sustainable healthcare NEWS 19 mins ago AIA Hong Kong & Macau hosted its Healthcare Financing Summit 2026 on Saturday, bringing together government officials, regulators, healthcare providers, academics, financial planners, and industry stakeholders to advance cross-sector collaboration. At the event, the insurer unveiled the Omni Healthcare Circle, a new partnership model with private healthcare providers designed to improve care quality, encourage appropriate and efficient use of medical resources, and support the long-term sustainability of Hong Kong's healthcare system. ## Summit addresses rising medical costs and cross-sector solutions Speakers at the summit included Secretary for Health Lo Chung-mau, Insurance Authority Chief Executive Officer Clement Cheung Wan-ching, and Permanent Secretary for Health Thomas Chan, who shared views on the future direction of Hong Kong's healthcare ecosystem. AIA Group Chief Executive and President Lee Yuan Siong also addressed attendees, reaffirming the group's commitment to supporting the sustainable development of healthcare in the city. The gathering comes amid mounting pressure on healthcare financing in Hong Kong. Research commissioned by The Hong Kong Federation of Insurers and conducted by the Centre for Ageing and Healthcare Management Research at PolyU CPCE found that private medical insurance spending rose by more than 60 percent between 2019 and 2023, while inpatient claim frequency climbed by 68 percent over the same period. AIA Hong Kong & Macau Chief Executive Officer Alger Fung noted that insurers, healthcare providers, and other stakeholders each play a vital role in keeping quality healthcare accessible and affordable as life expectancy rises and medical needs evolve. He added that the summit aims to unite different parts of the ecosystem around shared challenges and drive meaningful progress through closer provider collaboration and healthcare financing innovation. ## Three pillars of the Omni Healthcare Circle The Omni Healthcare Circle pairs clinical expertise with insights into healthcare utilization and patient journeys to help patients navigate treatment paths and anticipate costs more clearly. The initiative focuses on three core areas to support better health outcomes and patient experiences. First, it seeks to broaden access to high-quality and appropriate care by connecting patients with evidence-based care pathways aligned with clinical guidelines from the Institute for Medical Advancement and Clinical Excellence and recognized international standards, offering greater consistency and predictability. Second, it aims to give patients greater transparency and confidence through clearer, more objective information on care quality, outcomes, and efficiency so individuals can make informed decisions. Third, it is designed to support timely treatment and a smoother experience by bringing providers and AIA together earlier in the patient journey to provide greater certainty around treatment plans and expected expenses while streamlining administrative processes. ## Initial hospital partners and industry dialogue CUHK Medical Centre and Gleneagles Hospital Hong Kong are the first private healthcare institutions exploring the model with AIA, with the insurer remaining open to partnering with additional like-minded private providers in the future. Alice Liang, Chief Proposition and Healthcare Officer at AIA Hong Kong & Macau, explained that the initiative translates collaboration into practical action. She noted that both hospitals have strong ties to leading Hong Kong universities, bringing strengths in clinical care, research, and innovative medical technologies that help use medical resources more efficiently while extending benefits to patients and the wider community. The summit also featured panel discussions in which leaders from healthcare, insurance, and related fields exchanged views on applying the Omni Healthcare Circle model to foster greater transparency and more predictable patient journeys.

KV Cache Offloading over CXL is a new AI memory technology that helps AI data centers place and share memory efficiently according to demand. It adds a CXL memory pool to an AI memory hierarchy that previously consisted only of HBM* and DRAM: KV caches that will be used soon are placed first in HBM and DRAM, while KV caches to be recalled later are kept in the CXL memory pool. Because the storage location is determined by weighing factors such as reuse frequency, recency of use, size, and the cost of restoration, the approach can deliver benefits beyond a simple increase in capacity, and the memory pool can be used to reallocate resources in line with changing demand or to let multiple hosts share capacity. # (2nd LD) Appeals court upholds Kakao founder's acquittal on stock price manipulation charges Kim Eun-jung All News 13:27 November 20, 2026 (ATTN: UPDATES with Kakao's response in last two paras) SEOUL, Nov. 20 (Yonhap) -- An appeals court on Friday upheld a lower court's acquittal of Kim Beom-su, founder of tech giant Kakao Corp., on stock price manipulation charges related to the company's 2023 takeover of K-pop agency SM Entertainment. Kim was indicted on charges of violating the Capital Market Act by allegedly inflating SM share prices above rival Hybe's tender offer price through mass purchases in February 2023 in order to block Hybe's takeover of SM. The Seoul High Court upheld the lower court's acquittal of Kim, citing insufficient evidence. Kim Beom-su (C), founder of tech giant Kakao Corp., arrives at the Seoul High Court on Nov. 20, 2026, to attend his sentencing hearing on stock manipulation charges. (Yonhap) "The evidence presented by prosecutors did not prove that the defendants had intent to manipulate or stabilize share prices through artificial means or conspired to do so," the bench said. It said every stock transaction has the possibility of affecting the market price, noting that it would be unfair to punish all market purchases just because it might have impacted the price. The Seoul Southern District Court acquitted Kim in October last year, ruling that just because Kakao's mass purchase of SM shares affected their price, it could not be seen as price manipulation. After the appellate ruling, Kim told reporters that he would now focus his efforts on Kakao's new projects. Kim currently serves as the head of Kakao's Future Initiative Center. Prosecutors had sought a 15-year prison term and a fine of 500 million won (US$374,000) for Kim. Kakao welcomed the ruling, expressing hope that Kim would be able to better support the company's future growth strategies now that his legal risks have been resolved. "I hope today's ruling will ease concerns surrounding Kakao and lay the groundwork for rebuilding public trust," Kakao CEO Chung Shin-a said in a message to employees. yunhwanchae@yna.co.kr (END)
